strategy.title: No plan: the workbook has no price open-source maintainers are shown to pay
strategy.why: The only opening's 'price' is the $500 the huntr bounty platform pays security researchers per valid vulnerability report. That is a bounty, paid by a platform to researchers, not a purchase price paid by maintainers for an audit workbook. Without an evidenced price no plan can be shown to carry $3,000; every other link (reach, dated demand, measured pre-order conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet, $5 cost, 5-day settlement) is evidenced.

alternatives.title: Sell the workbook at $500 to 6 maintainers
alternatives.why: Rejected: $500 is a bounty paid to researchers by huntr, not a price maintainers pay for this workbook, so the target would rest on an unevidenced price.

alternatives.title: Submit vulnerability reports to huntr for bounties
alternatives.why: Not the opening on record and a bounty is not a purchase; Brain holds no evidence of valid findings or payout timing inside 30 days.

noPlan.decisiveGap: OFFER_AND_PRICE: no price that open-source maintainers are shown to pay for the audit workbook. The card's $500 is a bounty huntr pays researchers per vulnerability report - a different payer and not a purchase price.
noPlan.resolution: Brain researches the parked revenueRange question (what maintainers or their sponsors publicly pay for dependency vulnerability audits, with source and date); with an evidenced price, re-run the plan, which then needs ceil(3000/price) sales from 1,500 reachable projects at the measured 10% conversion.

excluded.why: No evidenced purchase price: the $500 on the card is a bounty paid to researchers, not a price maintainers pay

review.reasons: NO_PLAN is right. The card's only 'price' is the $500 bounty huntr pays security researchers per valid report: a bounty from a platform to a different payee, not a purchase price open-source maintainers pay for an audit workbook. Without it no deal count to $3,000 exists. Reach, dated demand, the offer's own measured 10% paid pre-order conversion, Brain-proved spreadsheet delivery at $5 and 5-day settlement are evidenced; the decisive gap is correctly OFFER_AND_PRICE, not a constraint. The bounty-hunting alternative is correctly rejected as a different opening with no evidence.
